Accordingly, the present study aimed to examine the relationship between the subcortical functional connectivity (FC) and treatment outcomes in schizophrenia using multivariate analytical approaches and machine learning algorithms. METHODS: One hundred and nineteen individuals with first-episode schizophrenia were recruited for this study. All patients underwent MRI scanning and completed assessments with the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) at baseline and at follow-up after 12 weeks of antipsychotic medication. We employed partial least squares analysis to explore the multivariate associations between changes in subcortical FC (∆FC) and changes in symptom severity (∆PANSS). In addition, a machine learning algorithm was used to predict the antipsychotic treatment outcome based on the distinctive subcortical FC pattern at baseline. RESULTS: We identified a distinctive subcortical FC pattern dominated by the striatum that was associated with overall treatment outcomes in first-episode schizophrenia. Furthermore, the reduction in PANSS total scores predicted using baseline subcortical FC patterns was positively correlated with the actual reduction in PANSS total scores following antipsychotic treatment. CONCLUSION: These results indicate that the distinctive subcortical FC pattern holds promise as a biomarker for schizophrenia, supporting individualized treatment approaches and facilitating early intervention to improve clinical outcomes.

title: Identifying GADD45A as a Potential R-Loop Regulator in Sepsis Via Machine-Learning and Multi-Omics Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome characterized by dysregulated immune responses, while the molecular basis of immune dysfunction remains unclear. Increasing evidence suggests that R-loop accumulation and DNA damage may contribute to immune disorders, but their roles in sepsis have not been systematically investigated. METHODS: Four Gene Expression Omnibus microarray datasets were integrated after batch-effect correction and normalization. Differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis were performed to identify sepsis-related genes. Overlapping R-loop-related genes (RLRGs) were obtained by intersecting differentially expressed genes, key module genes, and curated RLRGs. Machine learning was then applied to prioritize hub genes and construct an optimal diagnostic model, which was validated in external cohorts. A nomogram, single-cell RNA sequencing analysis, survival analysis, and in vivo / in vitro experiments were further used for validation. RESULTS: Five overlapping RLRGs ( EXOSC4, GADD45A, HMGB2, LDHA , and PRKDC ) were identified, and all were consistently retained by top-performing machine learning models, supporting their robustness. The five-gene nomogram showed good calibration and clinical utility. Single-cell analysis revealed cell-type-specific expression across neutrophils, monocytes, and T cells. Among the five genes, only GADD45A was significantly associated with poor survival. Experimental validation showed that GADD45A was upregulated in a cecal ligation and puncture-induced sepsis mouse model. In HL-60 cells, GADD45A silencing reduced lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammatory cytokine expression, R-loop accumulation, and DNA damage. CONCLUSIONS: GADD45A is a promising biomarker for the diagnosis and prognosis of sepsis and may promote disease progression by enhancing R-loop accumulation and DNA damage.

title: VI-RADS and beyond in bladder MRI: a pictorial review of quality control, response assessment, and artificial intelligence.
abstract: Management of bladder cancer changes markedly once a tumor invades the muscularis propria, making reliable separation of non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) from muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) a key clinical decision point. Multiparametric MRI (mpMRI), interpreted with the Vesical Imaging-Reporting and Data System (VI-RADS), standardizes local staging by integrating T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) with apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps, and dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI). As evidence has matured, the central challenge has shifted from diagnostic accuracy alone to implementation and clinical utility: ensuring interpretable image quality across scanners and workflows, reducing inter-reader variability, and translating VI-RADS categories into appropriate clinical pathways. Bladder MRI is also being evaluated for treatment response assessment after neoadjuvant systemic therapy and bladder-preserving approaches, supported by emerging post-therapy scoring systems such as nacVI-RADS, quantitative biomarkers, and machine-learning methods. The VI-RADS Quality Score and related quality-control concepts may help separate technically inadequate examinations from biologically equivocal cases. Near-term artificial intelligence applications are likely to be most useful for scan acceleration, automated quality auditing, semi-automated segmentation, and reader support for equivocal lesions. This narrative review synthesizes acquisition and interpretation essentials, diagnostic performance, recurrent pitfalls, and scalable solutions for VI-RADS implementation, response assessment, radiomics, and artificial intelligence.

title: Environmental exposure-integrated risk stratification for adverse outcomes after acute coronary syndrome: a multi-cohort machine learning approach.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) causes substantial post-discharge mortality. Ambient air pollution and meteorological conditions are associated with recurrent cardiovascular events, but existing clinical risk scores rely only on static admission parameters without incorporating post-discharge environmental exposures. Most machine learning (ML) models for ACS prognosis are single-center, single-horizon, fail to integrate both meteorological and air-quality variables, and lack external validation or interpretability. METHODS: We developed an interpretable multi-horizon ML framework for 3-month, 6-month, and 1-year post-discharge mortality using 24,120 ACS patients from 28 institutions in the Tianjin Chest Pain Center registry, split into training (n = 15,436), internal validation (n = 3,860), and single-region, multi-institution external validation (n = 4,824) cohorts. Seventeen predictors (3 demographic/clinical, 14 environmental) were evaluated across 5 algorithms. Discrimination was assessed by AUC (95% CI, DeLong method), calibration by Brier scores and calibration plots, and survival differences by log-rank test. Missing data were handled via multiple imputation, with SHAP analysis quantifying predictor contributions. RESULTS: CatBoost demonstrated the most stable cross-cohort performance, with 1-year AUCs of 0.625 (0.596-0.654) and 0.629 (0.602-0.654) in internal and external validation, significantly outperforming random forest and XGBoost (P < 0.05). Top predictors included winter minimum relative humidity, length of hospital stay, summer mean temperature, sex, and annual PM2.5. Predefined risk thresholds yielded significantly separated Kaplan-Meier curves (log-rank P < 0.001). Given missing key admission-severity indicators (Killip class, cardiac biomarkers, ECG findings), SHAP-based rankings are conditional on the available feature set and may overstate environmental exposures' relative contribution. CONCLUSIONS: With moderate discrimination (AUC 0.62-0.65) and single-region design, this multi-horizon ML framework integrating meteorological and air-quality variables was validated via single-region, multi-institution external validation. It is intended as a low-cost triage signal to prioritize follow-up, not a stand-alone decision tool, and does not replace clinical judgment. Cross-regional validation is required.

title: The application of artificial intelligence in healthcare practice: A mapping review of systematic reviews.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming healthcare practice, with growing evidence supporting its use in diagnosis, prognosis, treatment planning, and operational decision-making. The proliferation of systematic reviews in recent years underscores the need for an updated synthesis of the literature to inform research, policy, and practice. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and CINAHL for systematic reviews and meta-analyses published between 2019 and February 2026. Eligible reviews focused on AI applications in healthcare practice, were peer-reviewed, and written in English. A total of 368 reviews met the inclusion criteria. Publication volume increased steadily, peaking in 2025. AI research was concentrated in high-density domains, such as radiology, oncology, and critical care. Across reviews, diagnostic imaging, electronic health record (EHR) data, and biomarkers/laboratory results accounted for 68% of training data sources, though newer data types, such as wearable device and sensor data, emerged from 2022 onward. Diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment comprised over 80% of AI applications, with novel uses emerging in recent years, such as AI-assisted clinical documentation (e.g., ambient documentation tools) and patient education. Ethical concerns were reported in 78.5% of reviews, with privacy, model accuracy, data and algorithmic bias, and explainability as recurrent themes. The proportion of reviews reporting ethical concerns increased from 2021 to 2025. AI applications in healthcare are expanding in scope, diversifying in data sources, and evolving toward novel clinical and operational uses. The human-centered AI or augmented intelligence paradigm, integrating computational precision with clinical expertise, holds significant promise but will require parallel advances in governance, regulatory frameworks, and ethical oversight to ensure safe adoption.

title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence nominate PCLAF as a prognostic and druggable target for hepatitis B virus-associated hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: BACKGROUND: PCLAF (PCNA clamp-associated factor) is a protein involved in DNA replication and DNA repair. Aberrant PCLAF expression has been reported in multiple malignancies and is associated with tumor progression and poor clinical outcomes. However, the biological role of PCLAF in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains incompletely understood, particularly with respect to its relationship with the tumor immune microenvironment. Therefore, this study aimed to systematically investigate the clinical significance, biological functions, and therapeutic potential of PCLAF in HCC through integrated multi-omics analyses, experimental validation, and drug screening approaches. METHODS: In this study, an integrative multi-omics framework was employed to systematically investigate the molecular characteristics and biological functions of PCLAF in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Transcriptomic datasets from the GEO database (GSE83148 and GSE121248) and the TCGA-LIHC cohort were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes, followed by protein-protein interaction network construction and machine learning algorithms to screen and validate key hub genes. Pan-cancer analysis, clinicopathological correlation analysis, survival analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis were subsequently performed to evaluate the clinical significance of PCLAF. Single-cell RNA sequencing data (GSE202642) were analyzed to characterize the cellular heterogeneity of hepatitis B virus-associated HCC and identify PCLAF-associated cell populations. Functional module scoring and gene set enrichment analysis were performed to investigate the biological features of Cycling T cells. Spatial transcriptomic data (GSE245908) were integrated with deconvolution, cell-cell communication, and spatial regulatory analyses to explore the spatial distribution patterns and intercellular interactions associated with PCLAF. To identify potential therapeutic agents targeting PCLAF, virtual drug screening, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were conducted. Finally, clinical specimens and HCC cell lines were used for experimental validation. Immunohistochemistry, RT-qPCR, western blotting, colony formation, wound-healing, Transwell migration, and CCK-8 assays were performed to evaluate the effects of PCLAF on HCC cell proliferation and migration. RESULTS: Through integrated transcriptomic analysis, protein-protein interaction network construction, and machine learning approaches, PCLAF was identified as a key candidate gene associated with HCC. Pan-cancer and clinical analyses demonstrated that elevated PCLAF expression was associated with advanced tumor stage, higher pathological grade, and poor prognosis across multiple cancer types. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that PCLAF was predominantly enriched in Cycling T cells. Functional characterization showed that Cycling T cells exhibited a hyperproliferative but functionally restricted phenotype, characterized by enhanced proliferation accompanied by reduced activation and cytotoxicity. Spatial transcriptomic and cell-cell communication analyses further identified a potential epithelial cell-Cycling T cell interaction network, in which the MIF-CD74-CXCR4 signaling axis represented a major communication pathway. To explore therapeutic opportunities, AI-assisted drug screening, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were performed, leading to the identification of BRD-K12189280 as a promising candidate compound targeting PCLAF. Experimental validation confirmed that PCLAF was significantly overexpressed in HCC tissues, and its knockdown markedly inhibited the proliferation, migration, and viability of HCC cells in vitro. CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that PCLAF is significantly upregulated in HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma and promotes malignant cellular phenotypes. Multi-omics analyses revealed a close association between PCLAF expression and a hyperproliferative but functionally restricted Cycling T-cell state, highlighting a potential link between tumor progression and immune microenvironment remodeling. These results identify PCLAF as a promising prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in HCC, while BRD-K12189280 emerges as a potential candidate compound for future drug development.

title: Sex Hormone Receptors, HBV Integrations and Their Prognostic Predictive Value Among Hepatocellular Carcinoma Patients.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) related to hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection predominantly affects males, yet few studies have investigated the association between sex hormones and HBV integrations, and their involvement in HCC prognosis. We assessed estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) and androgen receptor (AR) expression via immunohistochemistry on tissue microarrays constructed from 426 HBV-related HCC samples. HBV integration features were determined using HBV-captured sequencing data. Logistic regression models were utilized to evaluate the association between sex hormone receptor expression level and HBV integration features. Cox regression models, combined with machine learning (ML) methods, were implemented to investigate the prognostic value of sex hormone receptors and HBV integrations concerning overall survival. We found high AR expression level was significantly associated with higher HBV integration levels (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.84, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.09-3.11, P for trend = 0.012), TERT integration (aOR = 2.34, 95% CI: 1.16-4.74, P for trend = 0.047), intergenic integration (aOR = 2.25, 95% CI: 1.20-4.24, P for trend = 0.021), and promoter integration (aOR = 1.81, 95% CI: 1.00-3.31, P for trend = 0.034). The inclusion of sex hormone receptors and HBV integrations in the predictive models led to improvements across all performance metrics in the Cox regression analyses (AUC improvement: 0.014 [Training], 0.026 [Validation]) and the ML (AUC improvement: 0.022 [Training]), although a slight deterioration in performance was noted in the ML validation set. The results suggested a relationship between AR expression level and HBV integration events, as well as the potential utility of HBV integration biomarkers and sex hormone receptor profiles in assessing post-surgical prognosis among HCC patients.

title: Machine learning prediction of childhood nephrotic syndrome outcomes.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Children with steroid-resistant, frequently relapsing, and steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome experience high disease and treatment-related morbidity. There are few prediction models for childhood nephrotic syndrome outcomes. Our aim was to develop and internally validate outcome prediction models, using machine learning methods. METHODS: We analyzed data from Insight into Nephrotic Syndrome: Investigating Genes, Health, and Therapeutics, a prospective observational childhood nephrotic syndrome cohort. We included children (1-18 years) diagnosed from 1996 to 2023 from the Greater Toronto Area, Canada, with baseline data from within 90 days of diagnosis. Outcomes were frequent relapses or steroid dependence by 1 year, relapse occurrence by 1 year, steroid-sparing medication initiation by 2 years, and initial steroid resistance. We developed and compared the performance of nine different machine learning algorithms for each outcome. Predictors included sociodemographic, clinical, and laboratory features. RESULTS: We included 515 children diagnosed with nephrotic syndrome. Of these, 484 (94%) were steroid-sensitive and 31 (6%) were steroid-resistant. Nine machine learning models were developed and optimized by hyperparameter tuning for each outcome. The random forest model had the best performance for predicting frequent relapses or steroid dependence, although its predictive ability was low (AUC 0.60). Machine learning models also had weak predictive ability for relapse occurrence (AUC 0.62; logistic regression with recursive feature elimination), steroid-sparing medication initiation (AUC 0.61; XGBoost), and steroid resistance (AUC 0.64; XGBoost). CONCLUSIONS: Routinely collected sociodemographic, clinical, and laboratory features at nephrotic syndrome diagnosis are weakly predictive of subsequent relapses and treatment response, using machine learning methods. Discovery of novel biomarkers may improve future prediction and proactive treatment.

title: Impact of hemoglobin glycation index and stress hyperglycemia ratio on short-term mortality in critically ill patients with heart failure: a retrospective cohort study using the MIMIC database.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: To evaluate the prognostic value of the combined assessment of hemoglobin glycation index (HGI) and stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) for short-term mortality in critically ill patients with heart failure (HF). METHODS AND RESULTS: ICU data on HF patients were retrospectively retrieved from the MIMIC-III and IV databases between 2001 and 2022. SHR and HGI were calculated at admission and stratified into tertiles. The endpoint was in-hospital and 90-day mortality. Logistic and Cox models evaluated associations between SHR, HGI, and their combination with mortality in both diabetic and non-diabetic patients. Exploratory interpretable machine learning prognostic models were developed to evaluate predictive performance. A total of 1573 HF patients were included. In-hospital and 90-day mortality rates were 14.1% and 24.3%, respectively. High SHR was independently associated with increased in-hospital mortality (OR: 2.01, 95% CI: 1.31-3.09) and 90-day mortality (HR: 1.54, 95% CI: 1.18-2.00). Higher HGI was associated with a reduced risk of in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.88, 95% CI: 0.78-0.99) and 90-day mortality (HR: 0.91, 95% CI: 0.84-0.98). High SHR and low HGI had the highest mortality risk for both in-hospital mortality (OR: 1.90, 95% CI: 1.288-2.85) and 90-day mortality (HR: 1.45, 95% CI: 1.13-1.87). The XGBoost model demonstrated optimal predictive accuracy, with an AUROC of 0.810 for in-hospital mortality and 0.808 for 90-day mortality. CONCLUSION: High SHR and low HGI are significantly associated with short-term mortality in HF patients, suggesting that their combined assessment may improve short-term prognostic assessment in critically ill patients with HF.
journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD

title: How machine learning applied on fMRI could improve the prognosis of the post-traumatic stress disorder: A systematic review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a stressor-related disorder that affects a significant proportion of the population worldwide. Despite the neurological nature of this disorder, its functional biomarkers, due to mixed results remain far to be understood. Therefore, the present review study aims to explore functional brain differences between individuals with PTSD and healthy controls with (TEHC) and without (TUHC) trauma exposure, using a machine learning approach. METHOD: A systematic search was performed in PubMed, Embase, and Scopus to identify relevant studies published before 1st of November 2024. A total of 19 studies were included in our data extraction process. The paper has been registered on OSF (https://archive.org/details/osf-registrations-n6bc7-v1)/(https://osf.io/n6bc7/). RESULTS: Default mode and salience networks have been determinant in classifying PTSD participants from both TEHC and TUHC. However, middle frontal gyrus as well as sensory motor area were only involved in classifying PTSD participants from TEHC. Finally, the results have also shown that the association between left amygdala and hippocampus is determinant in identification of PTSD severity. LIMITATIONS: The analysis of the available literature was restricted due to the non-homogeneous characteristics of studies - both in terms of methodology and clinical aspects - which restricted our ability to draw comprehensive conclusions. In addition, some studies used overlapping samples therefore limiting the generalizability of the results. CONCLUSION: The identified networks play a crucial role in distinguishing PTSD participants from healthy participants. These findings could aid in developing more accurate diagnostic tools and may even help predict individuals at higher risk of developing PTSD following exposure to trauma events.

title: Clinically interpretable nomogram incorporating radiomics and deep learning feature fusion from abdominal CT for preclinical type 2 diabetes.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop and externally validate a multimodal artificial intelligence framework for opportunistic detection of preclinical type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) from routine portal venous-phase abdominal CT in patients without recent laboratory testing. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study, 1257 adults without prior diabetes who underwent routine portal venous-phase abdominal CT were included. Patients were classified as preclinical T2DM or normal glucose tolerance based on fasting plasma glucose and oral glucose tolerance testing. Pancreatic segmentation was performed using an nnU-Net-based deep learning model with expert validation. From the segmented pancreas, 1708 Image Biomarker Standardization Initiative (IBSI)-compliant radiomic features were extracted following standardized preprocessing, reproducibility filtering, and ComBat harmonization. In parallel, multi-scale deep features were derived from five state-of-the-art encoder backbones, including transformer-based and segmentation-derived architectures. Clinical variables were incorporated to construct clinical-only, radiomics-only, deep-only, and multimodal fusion models. Six feature selection methods and five classifiers were systematically evaluated using stratified cross-validation. RESULTS: In 1257 patients (879 training, 378 external), preclinical T2DM cases were significantly older and had higher BMI, waist circumference, and glycemic indices than controls (all p < 0.001), with comparable demographics between cohorts despite protocol heterogeneity. Clinical-only models reached AUC 0.738. Radiomics improved discrimination (best AUC 0.792). Deep feature models performed better, led by MedFormer-v2 (AUC 0.834), significantly surpassing radiomics. Multimodal fusion achieved the highest external performance (best AUC 0.861). In a secondary analysis excluding all glycemic laboratory variables, the multimodal model still reached AUC 0.837, confirming the added value of imaging biomarkers for opportunistic detection. The stacking ensemble was well calibrated (AUC 0.856) and significantly outperformed three abdominal radiologists who evaluated CT images alone (mean AUC 0.671), while AI assistance improved readers' performance. CONCLUSIONS: Multimodal analysis of routine abdominal CT enables accurate and generalizable detection of preclinical T2DM, supporting opportunistic imaging-based metabolic risk assessment. A simplified nomogram was developed to support individualized risk estimation, although its interpretability remains partial due to the inclusion of a multimodal fusion score.

title: Prediction of Acute Liver Injury Trajectory in Patients Following Acetaminophen Overdose: A Multibiomarker Machine Learning Proof-of-Concept Study.
abstract: Clinical translation of novel therapies can be hindered by heterogeneity-driven sample size inflation in late-stage trials. In acetaminophen-induced liver injury (APAP DILI), many patients recover spontaneously, diluting investigational drug efficacy signals. We developed a prognostic enrichment tool to identify patients with worsening injury trajectories for more efficient trial designs. Biomarker model discovery and evaluation used serum samples from three UK cohorts: the MAPP2 APAP DILI biobank (n = 147), an independent pre-intervention evaluation cohort from the ongoing MAIL trial (n = 34), and healthy controls (n = 13). We measured 63 biomarkers and evaluated 321,682 combinations using kernel naïve Bayes classification to predict liver injury trajectory (ALT rising vs. falling). Sensitivity analysis using patient-level grouped cross-validation showed combining multiple biomarkers while constraining collinearity was necessary to maximize performance. A four-biomarker model (MCSFR, WBC, Sodium, K18) achieved AUC 0.868 (derivation) and 0.854 (evaluation). When optimized for prognostic certainty, the model yielded a Positive Likelihood Ratio of 14.4, increasing the Positive Predictive Value for worsening injury from a baseline of 29.4% to 85.7%. Time-dependent cost-minimization modeling for a hypothetical phase 3 trial identified an application threshold (sensitivity 80.0%, specificity 91.7%, Number Needed to Screen 3.4) as the global economic optimum, resulting in an illustrative trial cost reduction from $39.0 M to $8.3 M. This proof-of-concept demonstrates multidimensional biomarker models can resolve signal dilution. Distinguishing patients destined for injury progression reduces sample size requirements, which could de-risk novel therapy development.

title: Decoding tumor heterogeneity with imaging biomarkers predicts response to TACE plus immunotherapy and targeted therapy in HCC (CHANCE2204).
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: This study aims to quantify intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) and identify prognostic imaging biomarkers in patients with HCC treated with transarterial chemoembolization combined with immune checkpoint inhibitor plus molecular targeted therapy (TACE-ICI-MTT). APPROACH AND RESULTS: This multicenter cohort study included 742 patients with unresectable HCC who received first-line TACE-ICI-MTT from January 2018 to December 2022. Radiomic features representing global tumor regions (GTRs) and ITH were extracted from pretreatment CT scans. A composite GTR-ITH score was generated using principal component analysis to integrate both GTR- and ITH-related features. Ensemble learning with multiple machine learning algorithms was employed to predict treatment response. Model performance was evaluated by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Following feature selection, 17 GTR- and 27 ITH-related radiomic features were retained to construct the GTR-ITH score. The model demonstrated high discriminative performance, with AUCs of 0.94 in the training set, 0.82 in the internal validation set, and 0.83 in the independent test set. The GTR-ITH score was strongly associated with treatment response (OR: 34.39; p<0.001) and independently predicted overall survival (HR: 0.63; p=0.004). Patients classified as GTR-ITH low-risk consistently showed significantly prolonged progression-free survival and overall survival. To reveal the biological relevance of the radiomic score, immune infiltration patterns were characterized using bulk RNA sequencing data from the Cancer Imaging Archive. The GTR-ITH low-risk group also exhibited an immune-inflamed microenvironment characterized by enriched plasma cells and M1 macrophages, and reduced M2 macrophage infiltration. CONCLUSIONS: An imaging radiomic biomarker that captures both global and intratumoral heterogeneity robustly predicts response and survival in patients with HCC treated with TACE-ICI-MTT, and reflects underlying immune microenvironment phenotypes.

title: A Senescence-Related Signature for Risk Stratification and Predicted Immunotherapy Response in Breast Cancer: Integrative Pathology and Multi-Omics Analysis.
abstract: Cellular senescence exerts context-dependent effects on breast cancer progression and therapeutic response through dynamic interactions with the tumor microenvironment; however, its pathological manifestations, cellular organization, and clinical significance remain incompletely understood. In this study, we integrated whole-slide pathology images, bulk transcriptomic profiles, single-cell ribonucleic acid (RNA) sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and clinical data to systematically characterize senescence-associated features in breast cancer. Quantitative pathology and deep-learning features were extracted from hematoxylin and eosin-stained images, and a senescence-related signature (SRS) was constructed using machine-learning survival models. The SRS effectively stratified patients into distinct prognostic groups and showed consistent performance across the internally divided TCGA-BRCA subsets, with high-SRS patients exhibiting significantly poorer survival. Single-cell analyses revealed that senescence activity was predominantly enriched in epithelial and endothelial cells, whereas fibroblasts acted as major signal-sending populations and mediated enhanced collagen-related communication with tumor cells. Low-SRS tumors displayed greater immune-cell infiltration, higher immune-checkpoint expression, higher immunophenoscores, and more favorable Tumor Immune Dysfunction and Exclusion (TIDE)/immunophenoscore (IPS)-based predicted response profiles, while also exhibiting distinct drug-sensitivity profiles. Integrative pathological, transcriptomic, and spatial analyses further identified STARD10 as a senescence-associated candidate enriched in tumor regions and spatially concordant with senescence-marker expression at the spot level. Functional experiments showed that STARD10 knockdown reduced cellular metabolic activity in CCK-8 assays and suppressed migration and invasion, attenuated senescence-associated β-galactosidase staining and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)-related cytokine expression, and suppressed tumor growth in vivo. Collectively, these findings establish an integrated pathology- and multi-omics-derived senescence-related signature for prognostic stratification and characterization of TIDE/IPS-based predicted immunotherapy-response profiles in breast cancer, while identifying STARD10 as a candidate biomarker and a potential target for further mechanistic and therapeutic investigation.
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology

title: The Maternal Blood Transcriptome Reflects Molecular Signatures Associated With Large Offspring Syndrome and Other Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes in Cattle.
abstract: Large offspring syndrome (LOS) in cattle is a phenomenon characterized by fetal overgrowth that is largely associated with calves derived from in vitro produced embryos. Here it was tested whether occurrence of LOS as well as two other adverse pregnancy outcomes, stillbirth and abortion, could be predicted using changes in the maternal blood transcriptome early in gestation. Blood samples were collected from Holstein and crossbred heifers at 40-50 days of gestation following embryo transfer of in vitro produced embryos. A total of 203 samples were selected for RNA-sequencing and used to compare recipients of embryos resulting in live-born calves of normal birth weight (control; n = 96) with recipients of embryos resulting in LOS calves (n = 15), stillbirths (n = 43), and abortion before 210 days of gestation (n = 49). Large offspring syndrome was defined based on birth weights greater than 2 standard deviations from the mean. The number of differentially-expressed genes (p < 0.01) was 32, 176, and 100 for comparisons of control versus LOS, stillbirth and abortion, respectively. Biomarkers were identified in a randomly selected, balanced training dataset using Random Forest after filtering for differential expression. Markers were then tested in the held-out dataset through 6 machine learning models. The best biomarkers consisted of 26, 24, and 28 genes for LOS, stillbirth and abortion, respectively. The accuracy of prediction ranged from 0.91 to 0.965 for LOS, 0.73 to 0.98 for stillbirth, and 0.62 to 0.96 for abortion. Despite the relatively small sample size, the model demonstrated high sensitivity for LOS classification, supporting that the maternal blood transcriptome in early pregnancy reflects molecular alterations associated with fetal overgrowth that can be predictive of the condition.
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology

title: Early Prediction and Prognosis in Acute Kidney Injury Using a Biomarker-Aware Transformer: Retrospective Multicenter Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common, life-threatening complication among hospitalized patients. Timely prediction is crucial for prevention, while accurate prognosis following onset is essential for guiding care. Although electronic health records (EHRs) provide rich longitudinal data, their high dimensionality, heterogeneity, and temporal complexity pose challenges for traditional machine learning. OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to develop and evaluate a transformer-based model for generalizable AKI prediction and prognosis by modeling long-range temporal dependencies and complex relationships in heterogeneous EHR data and to examine its interpretability. METHODS: We developed the Biomarker-Aware Transformer for AKI (BAT-AKI), which integrates multidimensional embeddings capturing temporal dynamics, textual descriptions, hierarchical ontology structures, and semantic relationships in EHRs. To enhance sensitivity to AKI-related biomarker fluctuations, BAT-AKI combines masked language modeling with a novel biomarker abnormality-aware pretraining task. The model was pretrained and fine-tuned for 4 tasks: AKI onset, early reversal, recovery at discharge, and 90-day post-AKI mortality. Pretraining and internal validation used data from the National Patient-Centered Clinical Research Network (PCORnet) site, with external validation across 3 additional sites. RESULTS: BAT-AKI achieved the strongest overall discrimination, outperforming baseline models in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) on most tasks. For AKI onset prediction, it achieved an AUROC of 0.8549 (95% CI 0.8433-0.8658) and an AUPRC of 0.6041 (95% CI 0.5786-0.6292), exceeding the second-best baseline by 2.8% in AUROC and 8.1% in AUPRC. Across prognostic tasks, BAT-AKI achieved AUROCs of 0.6006 (95% CI 0.5703-0.6318), 0.6080 (95% CI 0.5745-0.6397), and 0.8017 (95% CI 0.7708-0.8311) and AUPRCs of 0.7036 (95% CI 0.6690-0.7388), 0.7417 (95% CI 0.7082-0.7765), and 0.5063 (95% CI 0.4422-0.5684) for early reversal, recovery at discharge, and 90-day post-AKI mortality, respectively, corresponding to relative gains of 2.4% to 6% in AUROC and 3.7% to 4.1% in AUPRC over the second-best baseline. Performance remained stable across external cohorts, with AKI onset AUROCs ranging from 0.7754 (95% CI 0.7677-0.7827) to 0.7989 (95% CI 0.7885-0.8092) and AUPRCs ranging from 0.4777 (95% CI 0.4631-0.4924) to 0.5687 (95% CI 0.5495-0.5871), corresponding to relative improvements of 3.7% to 5.3% in AUROC and 16.8% to 25.3% in AUPRC over the transformer baseline. In a low-resource setting using only 2% of the fine-tuning data, BAT-AKI achieved an AUROC of 0.7898 (95% CI 0.7759-0.8036) and an AUPRC of 0.4903 (95% CI 0.4640-0.5178) for AKI onset prediction, exceeding the second-best baseline by 4.2% in AUROC and 10.9% in AUPRC. Visualization of embeddings, attention patterns, and integrated-gradient feature attributions highlighted clinically meaningful relationships and patient-specific trajectories. CONCLUSIONS: BAT-AKI provides generalizable AKI prediction and prognosis with consistent discrimination across institutions, while offering interpretability insights into its predictions, supporting its potential for early warning and AKI care optimization.

title: [A multi-scale attention and federated learning-based method for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 immunohistochemical grading of breast cancer].
abstract: Immunohistochemistry (IHC) images for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) in breast cancer face challenges in cross-institutional sharing and suffer from insufficient representation of boundary categories. To address these issues, this paper proposes an automatic grading method that integrates multi-scale attention mechanisms with federated learning. Specifically, we construct a multi-scale attention residual network 50 (MSA-ResNet50) model, which enhances the model's discriminative capability for membrane staining intensity, staining continuity, and tissue morphological structures by fusing channel attention, spatial attention, and global attention branches in parallel. For the federated learning strategy, we incorporate client-side validation set accuracy and macro-averaged F1 score to perform quality-weighted aggregation based on the federated averaging (FedAvg) algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 87.78%, outperforming comparative methods. Furthermore, visualization results indicate that our model effectively strengthens feature responses in membrane staining regions that are critical for HER2 grading discrimination, thereby improving classification accuracy for the HER2 2+ category, which is clinically challenging to interpret. This work provides a technical reference for subsequent validation on real-world multi-center clinical data.

title: Precision medicine approaches in diabetic cardiomyopathy: from molecular mechanisms to personalized therapeutic strategies.
abstract: Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a distinct myocardial disease defined by the existence of abnormal myocardial structure and performance in diabetes mellitus patients without hypertension and coronary artery disease. DCM has been identified as a major cause of heart failure, hospitalisation and cardiovascular mortality with increasing global burden of diabetes. However, there is a large interindividual variation in disease susceptibility, disease progression and response to therapy, highlighting the limitations of conventional management strategies that are applied uniformly. Precision medicine provides a transformational approach through the integration of genomic, molecular, imaging, clinical and lifestyle data to allow for personalized risk assessment, early diagnosis, prognostication and treatment. This review presents the recent advances in the field of precision medicine for DCM with a focus on the molecular pathological mechanisms including metabolic disorders, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, fibrosis and microvascular injury. We discuss the relevance of genomics, pharmacogenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics and epigenomics in the context of disease heterogeneity and identification of novel therapeutic targets. Emerging biomarkers including circulating microRNAs, non-coding RNAs, inflammatory mediators, fibrosis-related markers and extracellular vesicles are discussed for their potential in personal diagnosis and prognosis. We also consider the increasing role of advanced cardiac imaging, digital phenotyping, wearable technologies, artificial intelligence, and machine learning in enhancing early detection and clinical decision-making. In this review, the therapeutic advances, including sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, anti-fibrotic therapies, mitochondrial-targeted interventions, regenerative medicine, gene therapy, and RNA-based therapeutics, are discussed, with a focus on the precision medicine approach. Finally, we present current challenges in data integration, clinical validation, cost-effectiveness, and ethical issues, and highlight future directions in digital twins, multi-omics integration, and AI-driven personalized cardiology. The combination of these technologies has the potential to revolutionize the prevention and management of diabetic cardiomyopathy and improve cardiovascular outcomes in patients with diabetes.
journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology

title: Machine learning-derived intracellular protein-based prognostic model reflecting a senescence-associated secretory phenotype-driven immunosuppressive microenvironment in lung adenocarcinoma.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate the associations of senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)-related genes with the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) and clinical outcomes in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and to develop and evaluate a prognostic signature for risk stratification and exploratory treatment-response prediction. METHODS: Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) was conducted to identify distinct molecular subtypes. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), Random Forest, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) were utilized to identify core prognostic SASP genes. The expression patterns of selected SASP-related genes were explored using multi-omics datasets, LUAD cell lines, and clinical specimens. RESULTS: Cluster 1 was associated with significantly shorter overall survival (OS), enhanced senescence pathway activity, and computationally inferred immunosuppressive and immune-exclusion features. Five intracellular SASP regulators-ANGPTL4, CDKN2A, H2AX, MMP1, and CCL20-were selected through machine learning to construct the SASP Protein Regulator Score (SASP-PRS). A high SASP-PRS was associated with the activation of senescence/SASP and cell-cycle pathways, suppression of antitumor immune signatures, and distinct immune-checkpoint and chemokine expression profiles. A higher SASP-PRS was also associated with advanced disease stage, poorer OS, predicted lower responsiveness to immunotherapy, lower predicted sensitivity to erlotinib, and higher predicted sensitivity to selected chemotherapeutic agents. The nomogram incorporating the SASP-PRS demonstrated discriminatory ability and calibration for predicting 1-, 3-, and 5-year OS in the analyzed LUAD cohorts. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that SASP-related gene-expression patterns are associated with LUAD molecular subtypes, senescence signaling, computationally inferred immune features, and treatment-related outcomes. The SASP-PRS may serve as a potential biomarker for prognostic stratification in LUAD. However, its utility for treatment-response assessment remains exploratory. Prospective external validation and functional studies are required to establish its clinical applicability and clarify the mechanisms linking SASP-related networks to the LUAD immune microenvironment.

title: Identification of Immuno-Diagnostic and Therapeutic Markers in Tumors and Inflammatory Diseases Based on Single-Cell and Machine Learning Methods.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chemotherapy is the mainstay of systemic treatment for colorectal cancer (CRC), but drug resistance and tumor heterogeneity markedly limit survival. Mitochondrial metabolism is increasingly recognized as a regulator of tumor progression, immune contexture, and therapeutic response. However, the prognostic relevance of mitochondrial metabolism-related transcriptional patterns and their relationships with chemotherapy-response signatures and immune features in CRC remain incompletely understood. METHODS: Clinical and transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas colorectal cancer cohort (TCGA-CRC) and Gene Expression Omnibus cohorts GSE17537 and GSE104645 were analyzed. A curated set of mitochondrial metabolism-related genes (MMRGs) were used to calculate an MMRG score, whereas genes upregulated in chemotherapy-sensitive cases in GSE104645 were used to derive a drug-sensitivity gene-set score by single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA). Weighted gene coexpression network analysis (WGCNA), differential expression analysis, univariate Cox regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, and multivariate Cox regression were used to construct a five-gene RiskScore. Prognostic associations were assessed using Kaplan-Meier curves, time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves, external validation, and subgroup analyses. Immune-cell enrichment and pRRophetic-predicted half-maximal inhibitory concentration values were evaluated, and CD36 was examined using in vitro phenotypic assays. RESULTS: Tumors showed lower MMRG scores than normal tissues, and higher MMRG scores were associated with better overall survival (OS). The drug-sensitivity gene-set score was higher in tumors but was not significantly associated with OS. A five-gene signature (CD36, CPA3, FCRL2, POU2F2, and S100B) generated a RiskScore that separated OS outcomes in the TCGA training, testing, and overall cohorts, as well as GSE17537, although its time-dependent discrimination varied across cohorts and follow-up periods. Similar survival associations were observed within subgroups defined by stage, age, and sex; however, independent or incremental prognostic value was not evaluated. High-risk tumors exhibited altered immune-cell enrichment, and the RiskScore was correlated with pRRophetic-predicted drug IC50 values after Benjamini-Hochberg correction. CD36 expression was higher in SW1116 than in NCM460 cells, and its knockdown inhibited proliferation, migration, and invasion. Mitochondrial function was not directly measured in these experiments. CONCLUSION: The five-gene RiskScore was associated with OS, immune-cell enrichment, and in silico drug-sensitivity estimates in CRC. It may serve as a candidate tool for prognostic stratification, but its incremental clinical value and treatment-predictive utility require prospective validation. The CD36 knockdown experiments support a tumor-promoting phenotype in SW1116 cells but do not establish dependence on mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming.

title: Cerebrospinal fluid amyloid and neurodegeneration biomarkers in the diagnosis and prognosis of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: a multicohort observational study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Neurofilament light chain (NfL) is an established biomarker for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). However, it remains unclear whether biomarkers reflecting amyloid-β metabolism (Aβ), tau (phosphorylated tau, pTau), and astrogliosis (glial fibrillary acidic protein, GFAP) can complement NfL in clinical applications. It is also unclear how Alzheimer's disease (AD) co-pathology affects disease progression in ALS. METHODS: We studied 264 patients with ALS and 164 disease-control participants, analysing baseline cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) NfL, Aβ peptides, pTau181, pTau217, and GFAP. A two-step diagnostic strategy was examined in individuals with intermediate NfL values, using machine-learning models. Prognostic associations were evaluated using linear mixed-effects and Cox models adjusted for established predictors; survival was additionally examined in pooled analyses including an external ALS cohort (n = 153). FINDINGS: Patients with ALS exhibited higher CSF NfL, Aβ38, Aβ40, Aβ42, pTau181, and pTau217 than controls, even within Aβ-negative subgroups. NfL discriminated ALS from controls with an AUC of 0.85 (0.82-0.88), which increased to 0.90 (0.88-0.92) in machine-learning models incorporating additional biomarkers. The machine-learning models maintained a high positive predictive value (0.90) for classifying cases with intermediate NfL values. Significant Aβ × NfL interactions were observed for longitudinal functional decline, and pooled survival analyses showed stronger associations between NfL and survival in the Aβ-positive ALS subgroup (14%) than in the Aβ-negative ALS subgroup (HR 4.02 [2.17-7.45] vs 1.62 [1.36-1.92]). INTERPRETATION: Multiple biomarker assessments can reduce misclassification of individuals with intermediate NfL values. CSF Aβ positivity modified the association between baseline NfL and disease progression. Personalised diagnosis and prognosis based on fine-grained co-pathology evaluation may enhance clinical management of ALS. FUNDING: This study was primarily supported by JST SPRING (JPMJSP2125). A complete list of funding organisations is provided in Acknowledgements.

title: Transcriptomics analysis and experimental assay to screen prognostic genes of N6-methyladenosine RNA methylation related to cuproptosis in colorectal cancer.
abstract: Cuproptosis and N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA methylation have been identified as significant factors in cancer. Consequently, we seek to uncover m6A RNA methylation-related prognostic genes that are correlated with cuproptosis-related genes (CRGs) in colorectal cancer (CRC) and develop an effective prognostic model. Based on public datasets, differential expression analysis, correlation analysis, and machine learning were conducted to identify prognostic genes. Subsequently, a prognostic model was constructed and validated. Furthermore, independent predictive markers were found through the use of clinical characteristics and risk score, to establish a prognostic nomogram. Prognostic gene expression in CRC and normal samples was evaluated using reverse transcription-quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). According to the prognostic genes, potential drugs for CRC were predicted using artificial intelligence drug design (AIDD) and computer-aided drug design (CADD). A prognostic model was developed utilizing 7 m6A RNA methylation-related prognostic genes that were significantly correlated with CRGs (MMP1, TIMP1, SNAI1, CDC25C, XRN2, COX5A, and FBXL5) in CRC. Survival analysis uncovered a notable contrast in survival outcomes between the high- and low-risk groups. The nomogram constructed based on age, stage, T stage, and risk scores demonstrated good predictive ability. RT-qPCR results showed that MMP1, TIMP1, SNAI1, and CDC25C were upregulated in CRC samples, while COX5A was downregulated, consistent with the bioinformatics analysis results. Furthermore, 186 candidate drugs targeting COX5A were identified, 153 of which showed better predicted binding affinity than the positive-control ligand 3,5‑diiodo‑L‑thyronine. Our analysis sets the groundwork for a more comprehensive comprehension of the fundamental molecular pathways involved in CRC.

title: Emerging role of AI in single-cell sequencing toward biomarker discovery, therapeutic target identification and precision medicine in lung cancer.
abstract: Lung cancer, the most common malignancy worldwide, exists in numerous histological subtypes, rendering the diagnosis and prognosis of the disease a challenge to clinicians. The recent technological breakthroughs in single-cell sequencing (SCS) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) have expanded the existing knowledge of lung cancer biology and provided new opportunities in the area of precision medicine. SCS has the potential to expose the enormous complexity of tumors, showing heterogeneous cell populations and characterizing the tumor microenvironment, and thereby overcoming the inherent limitations of conventional bulk sequencing in resolving tumor heterogeneity. At the same time, AI's advanced machine learning (ML) and predictive modeling capabilities, when applied to SCS data, can facilitate the identification of subtle cellular states, dynamic cellular interactions, and complex molecular pathways often undetectable by traditional statistical methods. This review examines the emerging applications of SCS and AI in lung cancer, focusing on biomarker discovery, therapeutic target identification, and precision medicine. We outline how their integration may support the identification of new biomarkers and therapeutic targets, with implications for more personalized treatment approaches. Integration of single-cell biology knowledge with AI-based analytics may assist scientists and clinicians in addressing the shortcomings of traditional approaches, which may offer personalized therapies with the potential to improve patient care. The ultimate goal of this review is to address the challenges and future perspectives of this emerging trend by focusing on the potential of these technologies to fulfill the unmet needs in lung cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment selection.

title: Exploratory clinical predictors and internally validated models of in-hospital mortality after PCI in obese patients with acute myocardial infarction and documented cardiogenic shock: a single-center retrospective study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Obese patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) remain at high risk of early mortality despite percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Obesity and related cardiometabolic disorders may aggravate vascular and microcirculatory dysfunction, potentially involving impaired endothelial cell function. However, prognostic evidence specifically focusing on obese patients with AMI-CS undergoing PCI remains limited. This exploratory, single-center study investigated clinical factors associated with in-hospital mortality and compared the predictive performance of logistic regression and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) using rigorous internal validation. METHODS: The archived analytic dataset contained 268 patients. After eligibility re-audit, three patients with body mass index (BMI) < 28 kg/m² were excluded, leaving 265 patients with documented AMI-CS treated with PCI. Seven routinely available candidate variables were evaluated in multivariable association and prediction analyses. Logistic regression and regularized XGBoost were compared using 20 repetitions of stratified five-fold nested cross-validation, with all model tuning confined to the inner training folds. Supplemental data on shock severity, serial lactate levels, vasoactive therapy, mechanical circulatory support, ventilation, renal replacement therapy, and hemodynamic variables were additionally evaluated descriptively and in a post hoc sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: Among 265 patients, 202 survived and 63 died during hospitalization. Higher heart rate, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, malignant arrhythmia, and multivessel disease were associated with in-hospital mortality. The seven-variable logistic regression model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.767 (95% CI, 0.696-0.831) and a Brier score of 0.152, compared with an AUC of 0.712 (95% CI, 0.641-0.779) and a Brier score of 0.169 for regularized XGBoost. Serial lactate concentrations at admission, peak, 6 h, 12 h, and 24 h were consistently higher in non-survivors, and cardiac power output was modestly lower. A post hoc severity-augmented logistic model achieved an AUC of 0.922 (95% CI, 0.888-0.951), but its calibration slope was 2.077, indicating that the model was not sufficiently calibrated for clinical deployment. CONCLUSIONS: In obese patients with AMI-CS undergoing PCI, heart rate, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, malignant arrhythmia, and multivessel disease were associated with in-hospital mortality. Logistic regression demonstrated more favorable internally validated predictive performance than regularized XGBoost using the same routinely available predictors. The associations of diabetes and hypertension, together with abnormalities in systemic perfusion, are biologically compatible with a potential contribution of endothelial cell dysfunction and impaired microvascular regulation; however, endothelial function was not directly measured in this study. External multicenter validation and studies incorporating endothelial biomarkers are warranted to further clarify the role of endothelial dysfunction in risk stratification for this high-risk population. These findings are exploratory and internally validated only; the modest sample size, absence of external validation, and originally outcome-informed nomination of the seven candidate predictors limit generalizability and preclude claims of clinical readiness.

title: Identification of Macrophage Polarization-Related Biomarkers in Multiple Myeloma Using Integrated Bioinformatics.
abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) is an incurable hematologic neoplasm with heterogeneous prognosis. Within the bone marrow microenvironment, macrophage polarization (MP) contributes to immune remodeling and may influence disease progression, yet MP-related prognostic biomarkers remain insufficiently characterized. In this study, we integrated transcriptomic data from UCSC Xena (n = 844) and GSE4581 (n = 414) to identify differentially expressed genes between immune-hot and immune-cold MM samples stratified by single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA)-derived immune scores. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and intersection with published MP-related genes yielded candidate genes, which were further refined using univariate Cox regression combined with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), eXtreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) and support vector machine recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE) machine learning algorithms to construct a prognostic model. An eight-gene signature (LGALS3, IL2RG, ADAM8, MERTK, ACSS1, ARSK, CBX6 and SOCS3) was established, demonstrating acceptable discriminatory ability for 1-, 2-, and 3-year overall survival (AUC 0.666-0.736 in training cohort). Risk groups differed significantly in immune infiltration patterns, predicted drug sensitivity, and survival outcomes. A predicted competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) network centered on MERTK and SOCS3 was also constructed. These findings identify eight MP-related hub genes as candidate prognostic biomarkers and provide a risk model with acceptable predictive performance, offering insights into the immune-metabolic interplay in MM and suggesting potential avenues for personalized therapeutic strategies.

title: Spatiotemporal atrophy subtypes in Alzheimer's disease: Neurodegenerative-vascular associations and potential prognostic value.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To characterize spatiotemporal atrophy subtypes in biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer's disease (AD) and examine their cognitive, vascular, molecular, and longitudinal correlates. METHODS: We applied Subtype and Stage Inference (SuStaIn) to baseline structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) from 484 amyloid-positive patients using 17 regional volumes. We compared subtype-specific cognition, cerebral small vessel disease burden, and post-baseline Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) trajectories; vascular risk factors and fluid biomarkers were exploratory. In a complete-case subset (45 patients; 134 observations), we compared SuStaIn with cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), plasma, hippocampal-volume, and combined-biomarker prognostic models. RESULTS: A four-subtype solution was reproducible across cross-validation folds (Bhattacharyya coefficient, 0.93): Typical (55%), Parietal-predominant (18%), Limbic-predominant (14%), and Hippocampal-sparing (13%). Higher SuStaIn stages correlated with lower baseline MMSE scores (ρ = -0.56). The Parietal-predominant subtype showed earlier onset, executive and visuospatial dysfunction, and rapid MMSE decline. The Limbic-predominant subtype showed delayed-recall and naming deficits. The Hippocampal-sparing subtype showed relative delayed-recall preservation, the highest adjusted deep white matter hyperintensity burden, and the lowest adjusted perivascular space count. It also had a higher adjusted CSF t-tau/Aβ42 ratio than the Typical and Parietal-predominant subtypes. SuStaIn showed the best in-sample prognostic performance based on marginal R² (0.579; comparator range, 0.239-0.483) and AIC. CONCLUSIONS: Biomarker-confirmed AD comprised internally reproducible atrophy trajectories with distinct cognitive, vascular, and molecular profiles. Spatiotemporal MRI may complement fluid biomarkers and conventional volumetry for patient stratification and prognosis. External validation is required to establish predictive generalizability.

title: Associations of cumulative exposure and longitudinal trajectories of neurofilament light chain with 1-year adverse events in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: A prospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Baseline neurofilament light chain (NFL) predicts amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) outcomes, but it does not summarize early repeated biomarker information. We evaluated whether cumulative NFL exposure (cuNFL), calculated over an early monitoring window, and longitudinal NFL trajectory groups were associated with subsequent adverse events in a prospective cohort. METHODS: This prospective study enrolled patients with ALS from 32 provinces in China between January 2024 and January 2025. Plasma NFL was measured at baseline, month 1, and month 2. We used K-means clustering to describe longitudinal NFL patterns and multivariable survival models to evaluate prognostic associations. Inverse-probability weighting and causal-forest analyses were used as exploratory, confounding-adjusted analyses of high versus low cuNFL. RESULTS: K-means clustering identified three longitudinal NFL groups: Low-Stable (n = 183), Moderate (n = 225), and High-Progressive (n = 100). The High-Progressive group had the shortest event-free survival (P < 0.001). Each 1-SD increment in cuNFL was associated with higher odds of adverse events (adjusted OR 1.99; 95% CI 1.52-2.60; P < 0.001). Using the manuscript-defined 127-event outcome, apparent discrimination was AUC 0.730 for cuNFL and 0.717 for baseline NFL. The paired DeLong comparison was not statistically significant (P = 0.084). Exploratory machine-learning analyses suggested heterogeneity in the association of high cuNFL with outcome by age and respiratory function. CONCLUSION: Early repeated NFL measurements summarized as cuNFL and longitudinal trajectory groups were associated with short-term adverse events in this cohort. These findings support further external validation of longitudinal NFL-based risk stratification. They do not establish a causal biological effect or a basis for routine repeated measurement.

title: Advances in microfluidic chip technologies for the study and management of gastrointestinal cancers.
abstract: Gastrointestinal cancers (GICs) remain a major global health burden due to late-stage diagnosis, limited therapeutic efficacy, and poor prognosis. Conventional diagnostic and treatment strategies are often invasive, costly, and lack real-time monitoring capabilities, highlighting the need for the innovative and patient-centered approaches. This review critically examines the recent advances in microfluidic chip technologies for the diagnosis, modeling, and treatment of GICs, including gastric, colorectal, liver, pancreatic, and esophageal cancers. Microfluidic platforms enable the precise manipulation of microscale fluids, offering advantages such as reduced reagent consumption, high sensitivity, and integration of multiplexed assays into portable systems. Notably, recent studies demonstrate diagnostic performance with area under the curve (AUC) values exceeding 0.90 and sensitivities approaching 90%, while detection limits for key biomarkers such as ctDNA and proteins have reached attomolar (10⁻¹⁸ M) and picogram-per-milliliter levels. Applications discussed include circulating tumor cell (CTC) isolation, exosome and ctDNA detection, tumor-on-chip models, and microfluidic drug delivery systems. In addition, advances in materials, fabrication techniques, and fluid dynamics are evaluated for their role in optimizing device performance. Emerging integrations with machine learning further enhance diagnostic accuracy and predictive capability. Despite these promising developments, challenges related to standardization, scalability, and clinical validation remain. Overall, microfluidic technologies represent a transformative platform for enabling rapid, minimally invasive, and highly sensitive approaches to cancer diagnosis and personalized therapy in gastrointestinal oncology.

title: Development and external validation of a non-laboratory model to predict early-onset cardiovascular disease risk: a multicohort machine learning study.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: This study aimed to develop and externally validate a questionnaire-based model for two related tasks in adults younger than 65 years: classification of incident early-onset cardiovascular disease (EOCVD) among participants without cardiovascular disease at baseline, and time-to-event prediction of all-cause mortality among participants with EOCVD at baseline. METHODS: Longitudinal data were obtained from CHARLS, HRS, KLoSA, ELSA, and SHARE. The incidence classification analysis included 37,082 participants, and the prognostic survival analysis included 19,478. Eighteen questionnaire or routinely obtainable predictors were used. No laboratory biomarker or imaging measurement was entered into either model, although reported diagnoses may have depended on earlier clinical testing. RESULTS: CatBoost achieved an AUROC of 0.6869, an AUPRC of 0.1438, a precision of 0.1105, and a recall of 0.6512 in the independent SHARE cohort. The Cox proportional hazards model achieved a test-set C-index of 0.7175; its 3-, 5-, and 7-year AUROCs were 0.7314, 0.7348, and 0.7350. CONCLUSIONS: P-EOCVD provides questionnaire-based risk stratification for incident EOCVD and subsequent mortality. Its low precision precludes diagnostic use. The model may support first-step screening where laboratory testing is not immediately available, but prospective validation and recalibration are required before use in under-resourced populations.

title: Interpretable Machine Learning Prognostic Model Integrating Inflammatory-Nutritional Biomarkers for Post-Prostatectomy Biochemical Recurrence: Development, Internal Validation, and Translational Target Exploration.
abstract: Objective: Biochemical recurrence (BCR) after laparoscopic radical prostatectomy (LRP) significantly affects the long-term survival of prostate cancer (PCa) patients. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning model integrating clinicopathological characteristics and preoperative inflammatory and nutritional indices to predict recurrence-free survival (RFS) and explore potential molecular therapeutic targets. Methods: A retrospective cohort of 320 PCa patients undergoing LRP at Beijing Chaoyang Hospital, Capital Medical University was analyzed. We integrated demographic, clinicopathological variables, and seven composite inflammatory/nutritional indices before LRP. A Mime-based machine learning survival pipeline was employed, combining Cox-based feature selection with survival algorithms. Model performance was evaluated using the concordance index (C-index), time-dependent ROC, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) was used for model interpretation and deriving clinical cutoffs. Furthermore, intersecting genes of BCR, lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), and prognostic nutritional index (PNI) were identified via GeneCards, followed by drug sensitivity screening and molecular docking. Results: The StepCox[both] combined with Random Survival Forest model demonstrated optimal performance, achieving a validation C-index of 0.788. SHAP analysis identified the top five predictive factors for recurrence: preoperative LMR, PNI score, postoperative Gleason score ≥ 8, positive surgical margin, and lymphovascular invasion. Model-derived cutoffs were determined as LMR = 3.9 and PNI = 48.8. Intersection analysis revealed 1211 shared targets among BCR, LMR, and PNI, with TP53 and PTEN ranking highest. Drug sensitivity analysis and molecular docking suggested potential inhibitory effects of compounds like sabutoclax and dordaviprone on these targets. Conclusions: The proposed model may serve as a robust and interpretable risk stratification for postoperative PCa patients. The integration of clinical phenotyping with exploratory molecular docking offers a translational pathway from prognostic indices to potential therapeutic hypotheses, warranting further prospective validation.

title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics combined with machine learning to unravel the heterogeneity of cholangiocarcinoma and the WFDC3-mediated prognostic regulatory mechanisms.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) exhibits substantial cellular heterogeneity and a complex tumor microenvironment (TME), contributing to poor clinical outcomes. Effective prognostic biomarkers and a deeper understanding of the cellular ecosystems associated with high-risk disease remain urgently needed. METHODS: We integrated five scRNA-seq datasets from GEO with four publicly available spatial transcriptomic sections and bulk transcriptomic data from the TCGA, fu-ICCA, and GEO cohorts. A multidimensional framework combining single-cell analysis, spatial transcriptomics, and machine learning was used to characterize cellular heterogeneity and identify prognostically relevant features. Hotspot was used to characterize T- and B-cell transcriptional modules, Scissor was applied to identify prognosis-associated malignant epithelial cells, and 101 machine-learning pipelines were evaluated to construct the ICCS prognostic signature. Cell-cell communication analysis and exploratory spatial co-density analysis were further performed to characterize ICCS-associated stromal-epithelial interactions, while in silico perturbation and functional assays were used to investigate WFDC3. RESULTS: The single-cell atlas identified 11 major cell populations and prognosis-associated T- and B-cell transcriptional programs. A six-gene ICCS comprising CEP55, EGLN3, GPRC5A, PRR15, SFN, and WFDC3 showed reproducible prognostic discrimination across the analyzed cohorts. ICCS-High displayed a markedly epithelial-dominant cellular composition, with epithelial cells increasing from 15.47% in ICCS-Low to 78.44% in ICCS-High, whereas T/NK cells decreased from 44.28% to 3.95%. Comparative cell-cell communication analysis revealed prominent mesenchymal-to-epithelial signaling enriched for collagen-related ligand-receptor interactions. COL4A1-CD44 showed the highest relative contribution and a more prominent mesenchymal-epithelial communication pattern in ICCS-High. Exploratory spatial density maps further identified local co-occurrence of mesenchymal and epithelial signals, supporting an ECM-associated microenvironmental context in the high-risk state. Separately, in silico WFDC3 perturbation implicated tumor-related pathways, and WFDC3 knockdown reduced colony formation, migration, and invasion of ICC cells. CONCLUSION: ICCS stratification captures distinct cellular and molecular states of the ICC microenvironment. The ICCS-High state is characterized by epithelial predominance, reduced T/NK-cell representation, and stronger inferred mesenchymal-to-epithelial collagen-related communication. COL4A1-CD44 and WFDC3 should be regarded as hypothesis-generating biological features requiring further mechanistic validation. ICCS remains a research-stage prognostic signature that requires standardized assays and independent prospective validation before clinical application.

title: Noninvasive diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease: a review of emerging biomarkers and multimodal approaches.
abstract: Noninvasive biomarkers are expanding access to biological assessment of Alzheimer's disease (AD). This review evaluates blood-based, neuroimaging, retinal, electrophysiological, digital, and behavioral measures alongside structured cognitive and functional assessment, and examines multimodal and machine-learning approaches for detection, differential diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring. Plasma phosphorylated tau, particularly p-tau217, currently offers the strongest scalable evidence for identifying amyloid and advanced tau pathology, whereas PET and MRI retain complementary roles in pathological confirmation, regional staging, exclusion of alternative causes, and characterization of atypical phenotypes. Retinal, electrophysiological, speech, sleep, and eye-tracking measures remain promising but require greater standardization and external validation. Across modalities, biomarker trajectories are temporally staggered, assay and platform differences affect interpretation, and pathology-phenotype mapping is modified by disease stage, cognitive reserve, copathology, vascular factors, and population characteristics. We therefore propose a phenotype-anchored, stepped pathway that begins with patient and informant history, objective cognitive and functional assessment, structural imaging, and routine laboratory evaluation; adds validated blood biomarkers when they resolve a defined uncertainty; and reserves CSF or PET for unresolved, atypical, or treatment-relevant cases. Discordant findings should prompt reassessment rather than automatic reclassification. We describe the literature-search and descriptive evidence-categorization approach used to select and categorize the evidence reviewed, and we place the findings within the emerging regulatory context of blood-based testing. Clinical translation will depend on harmonized thresholds, representative prospective cohorts, calibration, independent validation, and evidence that multimodal systems improve decisions and patient outcomes rather than benchmark accuracy alone.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

title: Deep learning-based histologic classifiers enable molecular subtyping of metastatic prostate cancer.
abstract: Metastatic prostate cancer is a clinically and molecularly heterogeneous disease. Under the selective pressure of androgen receptor-directed (AR-directed) therapies, resistant phenotypes frequently emerge, posing significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) is a clinically important phenotype characterized by lineage plasticity, neuroendocrine features, visceral metastases, and poor prognosis. Accurate diagnosis of NEPC remains difficult owing to its histologic and molecular complexity but has high clinical relevance. In this study, we developed a deep learning model that leverages interpretable cellular features to improve feature extraction from H&E-stained tissue sections (NEURAL-PC). By incorporating a multiple-instance learning framework, NEURAL-PC enables robust NEPC classification solely from H&E tumor images, achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.921 in independent external validation. In addition to its diagnostic utility, NEURAL-PC provides prognostic information that enables further subclassification of advanced prostate cancer across diverse datasets, supporting its strong prognostic value and generalizability. Broadly, our work highlights a hybrid approach that integrates features across different domains, offering a promising strategy for developing reliable deep learning tools in pathology. Built on this framework, NEURAL-PC represents an extensively validated diagnostic and prognostic model for advanced prostate cancer.

title: TRIM29 may facilitate progression of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma through immune remodeling.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly lethal malignancy characterized by late diagnosis, aggressive progression, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Biomarkers with both diagnostic value and biological relevance remain urgently needed. METHODS: Five Gene Expression Omnibus cohorts comprising 548 pancreatic samples were analyzed using differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and machine learning. Spatial and single-cell transcriptomics, immune infiltration estimates, and survival analyses complemented biomarker screening. Tripartite motif-containing 29 (TRIM29) was evaluated in 80 paired clinical specimens, knockdown and re-expression experiments, and subcutaneous and orthotopic KPC tumor models. RESULTS: Machine learning identified eight hub genes, including S100P, SFN, TMPRSS4, GJB2, GABRP, TRIM29, SERPINB5, and LAMB3, which showed favorable diagnostic performance across cohorts. Spatial transcriptomics revealed region-specific enrichment of these genes in PDAC tissues. Among them, TRIM29 was preferentially expressed in malignant epithelial cells, markedly upregulated in PDAC tissues, and associated with poor prognosis, reduced CD8+ T-cell infiltration, and activation of PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling. Functionally, TRIM29/Trim29 knockdown suppressed PDAC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, reduced AKT and mTOR phosphorylation, and increased CXCL10 transcript levels and extracellular protein concentrations. TRIM29 re-expression restored AKT and mTOR phosphorylation and reversed the increase in extracellular CXCL10 concentrations. In vivo, Trim29 knockdown suppressed tumor growth and increased CD8+ T-cell infiltration in orthotopic tumors. CONCLUSION: This study identifies TRIM29 as a machine learning-prioritized diagnostic biomarker and functional regulator of PDAC progression and immune remodeling, suggesting its potential value for biomarker-guided risk assessment and therapeutic exploration in PDAC.
journal: Pancreatology : official journal of the International Association of Pancreatology (IAP) ... [et al.]

title: Merging artificial intelligence and retinal vascular geometric parameters: A novel tool for diagnosis and prognosis prediction of diabetic nephropathy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is the leading cause of end-stage renal disease. The retinal microvasculature, as the only directly observable microvasculature, may reflect DN progression. This study aims to construct a non-invasive diagnostic and prognostic prediction model using the mixed effects of retinal vascular geometric parameters and clinical data. METHODS: We constructed a multimodal database including 397 patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease from multiple centers in China.
